articles.title: LLM Voice
articles.snippet: LLM Voice Refactoring Agile Architecture About Thoughtworks Topics Architecture Refactoring Agile Delivery Microservices Data Testing DSL about me About Books FAQ content Videos Content Index Fragments Board Games Photography Thoughtworks Home Insights Careers Radar Engineering follow RSS Mastodon LinkedIn Bluesky X BGG LLM Voice 29 October 2026 Martin Fowler Sometimes when I read a post, I get the growing feeling that I'm reading the output of an LLM. I can't necessarily define why, although there are the common tells (it's not the em-dashes, it's the load-bearing tapestries). As I do this my desire to read on atrophies, sometimes to the point of revulsion There are tools out there that claim to be able to tell the difference between LLM-written prose and the old-fashioned biological product. I'm wary of them, partly due skeptism about their accuracy, but also because it rather misses the point. The reaction to LLM-Voice is a human one, that sense that we are in an uncanny valley of prose. By the time I'd reach for a tool to tell me what I'm reading, it's already too late, even if it confidently tells me there's no LLM present. I'm also suspicious of my own ability to accurately recognize LLM voice. Language changes over time, so a common sign of age is complaining about the language of the youngs. I'm inclined to bristle at prose that talks about “adopting a new sales motion ,” or “a sharp round-up of news”. But I've heard these constructs coming out of human mouths, so that's more a generational difference rather than between carbon and silicon. (And as a transplanted Brit, don't get me started on Americanisms, I'm sure I'll get used to them momentarily.) Right now I urge authors to be extra-wary of LLM-Voice. In particular I strongly recommend that authors should not fall into the trap of getting the LLM to write a draft. Even if it's edited by a human, it's very hard to expel the LLM-Voice - thus causing the uncanny valley reaction. 1 Even accepting suggestions of rephrasing is dangerous. I have heard of people using LLMs to develop outline and structure, that may be ok, but only as far as an outline. 2 Authors should fill the prose themselves. 1: Very hard, but not impossible. I've come across one case where I do know the first draft was entirely done by LLM, but I detected no LLM Voice when I read the final piece. It did, however, need a professional editor at a major periodical publication to clean it up. 2: My policy on this site, is that anyone who uses AI to help them write should declare how they used it, usually in the acknowledgments. This is partly for transparency, and partly so that readers can learn useful ways to use AI. In my own case, I don't use AI for generating prose, nor for help in structure. The only way I use it for writing is as a search tool (but I verify any information by going to the source). Say Your Writing is even more important in the age of LLMs. I habitually speak the words in my head and then write them dow

articles.title: We ran AI agent swarms in Minecraft and Mindustry
articles.snippet: Agents in Games · Labs Home Projects QM Contact Agents in Games Minecraft Civ50 Bed Wars Mindustry The setup What we saw Funny bloopers Run your own swarm Open questions Agents in Games October 2026 Note: We're running a new Minecraft colony with 25 GPT-6.1 Terra agents. Follow on Twitch Understanding multi-agent dynamics is one of the most pressing challenges in AI alignment. Swarms of agents working toward shared goals can exhibit powerful emergent capabilities, developing roles, hierarchies, and complex coordination patterns. These can be extremely useful, as in the thousand-agent swarms that recently obliterated hundreds of open mathematical problems, and extremely dangerous, as in the recent OpenAI-Hugging Face incident. Like biology, studying agent dynamics requires both formal models (to describe the range of possible behaviors) and empirical research (to see what behaviors arise in practice). We teamed up with Olam Labs , which builds multi-agent environments for frontier labs, to run a series of experiments in Minecraft and Mindustry. Minecraft Minecraft is a natural environment for studying swarm behavior. Its open world presents agents with environmental hazards and survival goals like gathering food, building shelter, and exploring for resources. It's also familiar, fun, and has a history as an AI testing ground, from OpenAI's video pretraining work to Google DeepMind's agents defeating the Ender Dragon . We wanted long-running agents that could play Minecraft. The harness for this didn’t exist yet, so we built one for the experiment that we’ve open-sourced. Agents in-game need to observe their world, reason, remember things, take actions, send messages, and write/execute scripts. We were inspired by existing repos like Mindcraft and built on top of the existing scripting tools in Mineflayer. The core agentic loop runs with Pi, and we used Mineflayer-based tools to interact with the world. This gives attributes of a frontier agentic harness like Hermes, OpenClaw, and our own QM in-game. github.com/yc-software/minecraft-agent-harness Civ50 50 GPT-6.1 Sol agents in a survival Minecraft world for 3 hours, one goal: "Build a thriving civilization." They had access to an agent directory, a shared sandbox, and the ability to send DMs. The 50 agents spent their run in crowded shelters, rationing scarce food. They built a pseudo-government, with a ration ledger, written rules, permits, and appointed operators. They sent about 5,900 messages. At first things were very active. Agents spread out and started exploring their map. They were specifically fixated on harvesting trees. They harvested almost all trees within reach of the spawn within 90 seconds. A hierarchy was formed based on the directory order. Ada, who was first, became the de facto leader. Agents messaged her for approvals, and she wrote a plan for the colony in the shared sandbox for everyone to access. plans/settlement.md Download Settlement coordination (Ada) Primary storage Gre
articles.oneLineKo: Minecraft·Mindustry서 AI 에이전트 스웜 실험 공개
articles.summaryKo: YC Labs와 Olam Labs가 협업해 Minecraft와 Mindustry에서 다수의 AI 에이전트(GPT-6.1 기반)를 장시간 실행하며 멀티에이전트 상호작용을 관찰하는 실험을 진행했다. Civ50 실험에서는 50개 에이전트가 3시간 동안 생존 Minecraft 월드에서 '문명 건설'을 목표로 활동하며 배급 장부, 규칙, 허가증, 운영자 체계를 갖춘 유사 정부를 자발적으로 조직했다. 연구팀은 Mineflayer 기반의 자체 Minecraft 에이전트 하니스를 오픈소스로 공개했으며, Pi 에이전틱 루프 위에서 동작한다. 이 실험은 AI 정렬 연구 관점에서 에이전트 간 창발적 역할·위계·협력 패턴을 이해하기 위한 경험적 연구의 일환이다.

articles.oneLineKo: AI가 인용하는 통계 절반이 근거 없는 '좀비 스탯'
articles.summaryKo: Trakkr Research는 ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Google AI Overviews 등 5개 AI 어시스턴트에 200개의 질문을 던져 1,285개의 통계 인용을 추적했다. 그 결과 절반 미만만이 실제로 동일한 내용을 뒷받침하는 연구로 이어졌으며, 나머지는 출처가 불분명하거나 근거가 사라진 '좀비 스탯'이었다. 예시로 든 '영업사원의 44%가 첫 팔로업 후 포기한다'는 통계는 5개 AI 모두가 인용했지만 실제 연구 자료는 찾을 수 없었다. 이 연구는 AI가 인용하는 숫자의 신뢰성 문제를 지적한다.

articles.title: We're releasing the weights of Mistral Large 4
articles.snippet: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) is now open weight | Mistral Get in touch Menu Research Sovereign AI Cloud Customers Company Get in touch Login Why Sovereign AI Products Method Sovereign AI in practice Inference Compute Energy & utilities Manufacturing Financial services Public sector Cybersecurity All customers Blog Docs About us Careers Research Sovereign AI Cloud Customers Company Why Sovereign AI Products Method Sovereign AI in practice Inference Compute Energy & utilities Manufacturing Financial services Public sector Cybersecurity All customers Blog Docs About us Careers Get in touch --> Login Studio Vibe Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Built for Coders, Trusted by Defenders. Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Built for Coders, Trusted by Defenders. Back to Blog Share this post Copy url to clipboard Copied Thinking Summary Mistral released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model, now available with improved coding, cybersecurity, and reasoning efficiency. It leads open-weight benchmarks in coding and defensive security while offering three reasoning modes for cost-performance balance. Fully open-weight and European-trained, it empowers sovereign AI with customizable, self-hosted deployment options. We release the weights of Le Chonk, advancing the frontier of open models in agentic coding and cybersecurity. Earlier this month, we released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), our flagship 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal model, in public preview. The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations, and we're grateful to our developer community, early-access customers, and partners for their support, collaboration, and feedback. Since then, we've put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity . Gains continue to accelerate, with no signs of saturation. Today, we're releasing the weights of this improved Mistral Large 4. The new model also features substantial gains in reasoning efficiency that give developers greater performance while lowering inference costs. Mistral Large 4 ranks as the best open-weight model for coding and among the world's most capable open models overall. Trained from scratch on European infrastructure with clear lineage from inception to release, it gives organizations a trusted foundation for Sovereign AI Mistral is defining the sovereign AI category and leading the open frontier. We're committed to building the world's most capable models and releasing them openly, giving developers, enterprises, and institutions the power to own, customize, and control their AI. Built for the Builders. Mistral Large 4 entered public preview with strong results across leading coding benchmarks. Just three weeks of additional reinforcement learning have since propelled it to the forefront of open-weight coding, taking the lead on FrontierCode and Terminal-Bench while matching the best open-weight models on the Artificial Anal

articles.summaryKo: Mistral이 1조 파라미터 규모의 네이티브 멀티모달 모델 Mistral Large 4(Le Chonk)의 가중치를 공개했습니다. 프리뷰 공개 이후 강화학습을 추가로 진행해 코딩과 방어적 사이버보안 성능이 크게 향상되었으며, 오픈웨이트 모델 중 코딩 분야 최고 성능을 기록했습니다. 유럽 인프라에서 처음부터 학습되어 출처가 명확하며, 세 가지 추론 모드를 제공해 비용 대비 성능을 조절할 수 있습니다. Mistral은 이를 통해 소버린 AI 분야에서 신뢰 가능한 오픈 모델 기반을 제공하고자 합니다.

articles.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart
articles.snippet: DoorDash to Acquire Instacart to Help Local Stores Win | DoorDash DoorDash DoorDash Products Company Impact Advertise News Blog Help English (US) Español (US) English (CA) Français (CA) English (AU) English (NZ) US Get Started News Announcements Culture Policy Trends & Insights Archives Categories Announcements Culture Policy Trends & Insights Archives Announcements DoorDash to Acquire Instacart to Help Local Stores Win Together, DoorDash and Instacart would help stores of every size reach more customers with the kinds of innovative technology that the biggest online retailers and grocers build for themselves. Oct 29, 2026 Transaction values Instacart at $65.00 per share, representing a 26% premium to Instacart's closing price on October 22, 2026 Together, DoorDash and Instacart would help stores of every size reach more customers with the kinds of innovative technology that the biggest online retailers and grocers build for themselves Consumers to benefit from more choice and access to affordable delivery and savings Dashers and Shoppers to have more earnings opportunities and more choice over when and how they earn DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ: DASH) and Maplebear Inc. (d.b.a. Instacart, NASDAQ: CART) today announced a definitive agreement under which DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a total value of $65.00 for each Instacart share, or an equity value of approximately $17 billion. The aggregate transaction consideration will be at least 75% cash, with Instacart stockholders able to elect cash, DoorDash stock, or a combination of both, subject to proration so that DoorDash stock does not exceed 25% of the aggregate consideration. Instacart's board of directors has unanimously approved the agreement. DoorDash and Instacart share a mission to help local businesses succeed. Families turn to Instacart for the big weekly shop and to DoorDash for meals and nearly anything else they need from their neighborhood in under an hour. The combined company will offer grocers and retailers of every size DoorDash's delivery network and Instacart's grocery and fulfillment technology, in both apps and on stores' own websites, along with the advertising and AI tools each company has built. On either app, customers pick a store in their own community, and the store makes the sale. Consumers will have more stores to choose from, more savings opportunities when they choose to shop with a local business, and faster delivery options, while Dashers and Shoppers will have more ways to earn. Most grocery shopping still happens in stores, but more people are buying groceries and everyday goods online. They expect fast, affordable delivery and an easy way to order. The biggest online retailers and grocers are racing ahead, building their own delivery fleets, warehouses, membership programs, and AI shopping assistants. articles.title: H.264 Is Magic (2016)
articles.snippet: H.264 is magic: a technical walkthrough of a remarkable technology. Sid Bala Home LinkedIn GitHub Sign in Subscribe H.264 is Magic Sid Bala 02 Nov 2016 • 10 min read Share H.264 is a video compression codec standard. It is ubiquitous - internet video, Blu-ray, phones, security cameras, drones, everything. Everything uses H.264 now. H.264 is a remarkable piece of technology. It is the result of 30+ years of work with one single goal: To reduce the bandwidth required for transmission of full-motion video. Technically, it is very interesting. This post will give insight into some of the details at a high level - I hope to not bore you too much with the intricacies. Also note that many of the concepts explained here apply to video compression in general, and not just H.264. Why even compress anything? A simple uncompressed video file will contain an array of 2D buffers containing pixel data for each frame. So it's a 3D (2 spatial dimensions and 1 temporal) array of bytes. Each pixel takes 3 bytes to store - one byte each for the three primary colors (red, green and blue). 1080p @ 60 Hz = 1920x1080x60x3 => ~ 370 MB/sec of raw data. This is next to impossible to deal with. A 50GB Blu-ray disk will only hold ~2 mins. You can't move it anywhere fast. Even SSDs have trouble dumping this straight from RAM to Disk[^1]. So yeah. We need compression. Why H.264 compression? Yes, I will answer this. But first let me show you something. Here is the Apple Homepage: I captured the screen of this home page and produced two files: PNG screenshot of the Apple homepage 1015KB 5 Second 60fps H.264 video of the same Apple homepage 175KB Eh. What? Those file sizes look switched. No, they're right. The H.264 video, 300 frames long is 175KB. A single frame of that video in PNG is 1015KB. It looks like we're storing 300 times the amount of data in the video. But the file size is a fifth. So H.264 would seem to be 1500x as efficient as PNG. How is this even possible? All right, what's the trick? There are very many tricks! H.264 uses all the tricks you can think of (and tons you can't think of). Let's go through the important ones. Shedding weight Imagine you're building a car for street racing. You need to go faster. What is the first thing you do? You shed some weight. Your car weighs 3000 lbs. You throw away stuff you don't need. Those back seats? pfft. Chuck those. That subwoofer? Gone. No music for you. Air Conditioning? Yeah, ditch it. Transmission? Ye..no. Wait! We're gonna need that. You remove everything except the things that matter. This concept of throwing away bits you don't need to save space is called lossy compression. H.264 is a lossy codec - it throws away less important bits and only keeps the important bits. PNG is a lossless codec. It means that nothing is thrown away. articles.oneLineKo: H.264 압축 기술의 원리를 쉽게 풀어낸 해설
articles.summaryKo: 이 글은 H.264 비디오 코덱이 어떻게 방대한 압축률을 달성하는지 기술적으로 설명한다. 1080p 60fps 무압축 영상은 초당 약 370MB에 달하지만, H.264는 손실 압축(lossy compression)을 통해 PNG 스크린샷보다 훨씬 작은 용량으로 동일한 장면의 300프레임 영상을 담아낸다. 저자는 이를 경주용 자동차에서 불필요한 무게를 줄이는 것에 비유하며, 중요하지 않은 비트를 버리는 손실 압축과 비트 단위로 원본을 복원하는 PNG 같은 무손실 압축의 차이를 설명한다. 이후 H.264가 사용하는 구체적인 압축 기법들을 단계별로 다룬다.
